text: A CDN can reduce latency by far more than any QoS policy, because it attacks propagation delay rather than queueing delay.
explanation: True. QoS can shave a few milliseconds of queueing; moving content 8,000 km closer removes 150 ms of propagation, which Chapter 3 identified as otherwise irreducible. Caching and anycast have done more for perceived Internet performance than every QoS mechanism deployed.
